name: Midland West Manufacturing
old_description: Precision Machining & Fabrication Solutions Designed for Montana
about:
Midland West Manufacturing was founded in 1977 in Billings, Montana, by Stephen Pinnow and his father John Pinnow, starting with a single Miller Bobcat welder. The company moved through several smaller facilities before settling into its current 25,000-square-foot plant near the Lockwood Exit in 2006.

The shop combines fabrication, metal forming, machining, and design-build services under one roof. Its equipment lineup includes lathes, mills, press brakes, plate rolls, and fabricators, enabling structural, industrial, commercial, and custom fabrication; welding, handrailing, prototyping, and equipment repair; heavy-duty and CNC press brake work, plate and profile rolling, and straightening; traditional and CNC milling, metalizing, pipe threading, and line boring; plus SolidWorks CAD/CAM, shop drawings, design refinement, quoting, and material take-offs. The facility handles projects from one-off prototypes to high-production runs.

Midland West serves a diverse customer base across Montana and beyond, with noted work in agricultural equipment built for the state's plains and precision components for the aerospace sector. The company also supports industrial and commercial clients throughout Yellowstone County and the surrounding region.

The firm emphasizes its Montana heritage and community roots, positioning itself as more than a typical job shop. It cites quick turnaround times driven by in-house capabilities and industry connections, and claims the largest forming equipment in the region to take on jobs others cannot.
